explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates the finetuned NLI model (LLM-as-judge) against human evaluation through correlation analysis on four meta-evaluation datasets, reporting both Pearson and Spearman correlations

prompts.notes: The paper describes using NLI model to judge whether SCUs are entailed by system summaries using entailment probability or labels, but exact prompt templates are not shown

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: Filtered responses from noisy worker who disagreed with majority in 72% of cases

guidelines.notes: Paper mentions annotation instructions and interfaces shown to crowdsourcing workers, with Figure illustrating data annotation instructions

sample_size.notes: Validation conducted on 4 meta-evaluation datasets: TAC2008 (96 examples), TAC2009 (88 examples), REALSumm (100 examples), PyrXSum (100 examples) - total 384 examples evaluated by both LLM and human

quantitative_scores.notes: Lite 2 Pyramid outperforms other metrics by 0.08-0.16 higher summary-level correlations
Lite 2 Pyramid shows consistent advantage across datasets

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Correlation advantage of 0.08-0.16 considered substantial improvement

validation_results.summary_finding: Lite 2 Pyramid (LLM-as-judge) consistently achieves the best summary-level correlations (0.08-0.16 higher than other metrics) and demonstrates that the finetuned NLI model can generalize to new data examples as a reliable proxy for human judgment.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluate the same criterion - presence of Summary Content Units (SCUs) in system summaries
